warnings: This paper focuses on cadmium concentration, NOT zinc concentration in grain - primary outcome variables are grain yield and Cd concentration
Zinc is applied as a treatment but grain Zn concentration is NOT measured or reported
The study examines whether Zn application affects Cd concentration (potential antagonistic effect), not Zn biofortification
Multiple factorial treatments include N, P, and Zn in various combinations - need to isolate Zn vs no-Zn comparisons
Two cultivars (Medora and Sceptre) and two soil types analyzed separately - not valid statistical comparison between cultivars
Three-year study with significant year effects - data combined where treatment-by-year interaction not significant
WARNING: SCANNED PDF - Text may have OCR errors
WARNING: VAR-UNCLEAR - Variance type not clearly stated
recon.variance_source: SE values reported in all tables, e.g., 'SE 169.3' in Table 5
recon.treatment_definition: Various treatments including Zn application (Treatment 2: Zinc; Treatment 8: P-N Dual Band + Zn; Treatment 11: P Broad N Band + Zn)
recon.potential_tc_confusion: Multiple factorial combinations make it complex to isolate Zn effects - must use contrast analysis approach
recon.sample_size_source: Experimental design was a randomized complete block with four replications
recon.extraction_guidance: This paper does NOT contain the target outcome variable (grain Zn concentration) for the meta-analysis. The study focuses on cadmium concentration and yield effects. Zinc was applied as a treatment to test its effect on cadmium uptake, but grain zinc concentrations were not measured or reported. This paper should be excluded from the zinc biofortification meta-analysis.
